Title: It's that time of the year
NewsSummary: Alumnus Haider Ali shares a message for graduates and memories of his home away from home.
NewsContent:
It's been a year since his graduation from AKU, and Haider Ali, MBBS '18, can empathise with how this year's batch is likely to feel. "There's certainly a feeling of pride," Haider says. "But there also anxiety as the 'What's Next?' question starts to linger in everyone's mind."

He adds that there are a lot of other bittersweet experiences awaiting the graduating class. For example, Haider recalls how difficult it can be to leave one's hostel room. Room 178 in the Male Hostel had been Haider's home away from home for five years. In fact, Haider remembers missing his 'own place' even when he was back home with his parents during semester break.

But the biggest change will be being away from friends you've lived and studied with for years, many of whom Haider feels are like family. During his years on campus, Haider and his friends spent hours hanging out in each other's hostel room. A striking memory is of the all-nighters fueled by their favourite energy drink from the convenience store nearby: one of many rituals he had grown accustomed to. 

Haider also remembers his bond with another member of the #AKUfamily: the Male Hostel cook, Zubair, who like a parent, would ensure that he didn't miss a meal as he rushed between classes and lectures. "I'd always leave my room key with Zubair. On my return, there would be a delicious meal waiting for me." 

Thankfully, Haider didn't miss campus life for too long after his graduation as he started his first job straight after at AKU's Critical Creative Innovative Thinking Forum (CCIT) at the Stadium Road campus. As a coordinator at CCIT, Haider is helping developing an ecosystem of innovation at AKU by building partnerships and connections between the brightest minds in industry and AKU staff, students and faculty developing new ideas in biomedicine and healthcare.

"It may feel like everyone is going their own way but don't forget that there's a family with you right here," says Haider. "I'm fortunate that I never had to feel that sense of displacement but trust me you'll never lose touch with your dearest friends. And I can vouch for the fact you'll love seeing those familiar faces and special friends whenever you return to campus."
